description: Changes the cadence of ONE campaign: the shared template every person gets, and people added later. A change of form or tone (lowercase, more formal, shorter, another greeting, no emoji) applies to every step. A change of content or structure (add a question, mention something, change the argument) applies to the step it points to (a day, a channel, a sentence only that step has), not to every step, unless it is about every message. Each follow-up keeps its own new reason to reply (a case, how the work is done, a resource, what changes for the reader), and the last step keeps closing the subject. requestedDays lists the steps the request covers; edits on any other day are refused (a new step, op add, always fits). To change one or a few steps, pass `edits` (day or "last", optional channel, new body; op add/remove/move to insert, delete or reschedule a step, op condition to change what lets a step go: no reply in N days, the invite accepted, or the e-mail before it opened) and the other steps stay as they are; `steps` replaces the whole cadence. A step may carry `variantB` (a version B for an A/B test, subject for e-mail only): it is saved with the exact text given, never rewritten, in the same place as a version B made on the cadence screen; an edit with only variantB leaves version A as it is, and variantB null removes it. A LinkedIn connection request and a like step take no version B (the result lists them in versionBNotSaved). With both, edits win and steps is ignored; a call that carries every text twice can be cut off. scope is "template" (the default) for any wording change, including 'the template', 'every day' or 'everyone', even while the screen shows one example person; "one_person" with prospectId changes only that one person's messages. A prospectId without scope "one_person" is ignored. Does not activate sending. A template change saves the template only: the people's steps not sent yet take it with its fields to write, and nobody is written again until a rewrite is requested (messagesNext in the result says how). applyTo says who a template change reaches: pending (the default) is everyone on the current numbered version, each from where they are, what was sent never changing; new_only ends the current version, so who already started it finishes it as it was, and the change becomes version N+1 for who has not started and who enters from now on (endedVersion in the result). People on an earlier version never change.

applyTo.description: Who a template change reaches. pending (default): everyone on the current numbered version, each from where they are. new_only: who already started finishes the current version as it was; the change is a new numbered version for who has not started and who enters from now on.

edits.description: Steps to change; every other step is kept.

body.description: New message body, for change and add. Use {{firstName}}, {{company}}, {{headline}}, {{signal}} and {{senderFirstName}} for a campaign-wide change. {{outroDecisor}} is the first name of another decision maker at the person's own company (found by Nock, never invented), for a short follow-up such as 'Oi, {{firstName}}, isso é algo que você olharia ou fica mais com o {{outroDecisor}}?'; a person with none gets the sentence without a name ('...ou tem outra pessoa aí que cuida disso?') or the step's outroDecisorFallback.

branch.description: Pick (or, for add, put) the step on this path after the LinkedIn invite. The path after the LinkedIn invite (only when the cadence has a LinkedIn message after the invite and e-mails or WhatsApp after it): accepted ("Aceitou o convite": the LinkedIn message first, then any steps for who accepted) or not_accepted ("Não aceitou em X dias": e-mails or WhatsApp for who did not accept; X is its first step's day minus the invite's, 1 to 21; never a LinkedIn step). Each person goes down one path. Steps on no path go first, then accepted, then not_accepted. Keep each step's branch as the campaign has it; a cadence sent without branches, with a LinkedIn message waiting for the accept before e-mails, gets the paths by itself.

channel.description: Pick the step on this channel (with "last": the final step on this channel). Required for add. whatsapp_task is a WhatsApp step the person's sender sends from their own phone: a task on the WhatsApp screen, never sent by Nock, only for workspaces that have it (the save refuses it otherwise). linkedin_like is "Curtir post": Nock likes the newest LinkedIn post the person wrote from the campaign's LinkedIn account, a warm touch before the invite or a message; body empty, no subject; skipped when they posted nothing recent; to have the invite go some hours after the like, give the invite condition no_reply_hours (2 hours is the usual). Only on request and only for workspaces that have it (the save refuses it otherwise)."Curtir post" likes only a post she wrote in recentDays (30 by default); with none it is skipped, unless commentFallback is true (off by default), when it likes her recent comment instead. like_post is an old name of it with commentFallback false. A linkedin_like step can do another interaction (interaction): like_comment (her recent comment, never on the post she was found on nor a watched competitor's), visit (a profile view she is told about) or reply_comment (a short public reply the Nock Agent writes from her comment, approved in the Inbox unless sending is automatic). No follow step exists.

commentFallback.description: linkedin_like "Curtir post" (no interaction or like) only: true likes her newest recent comment when she wrote no post in recentDays (never a comment on the post she was found on nor on a post of someone the campaign's signal watches); false (the default for a new step) skips the step then and the cadence goes on. The cadence read with the campaign shows each step's commentFallback as it goes out: keep it when the steps are sent back. With add, the new step's choice (off when omitted); with change on a linkedin_like step, its new one.

condition.description: op condition only: the step's new condition (read with no other op). What lets this step go after the one before. no_reply_days (the default): it goes on its day if there is no reply; no_reply_hours: it goes waitHours (1 to 72) after the step before was sent, if there is no reply, and its day is set from that step; invite_accepted: a LinkedIn message right after the invite, after the accept (automatic there); email_opened: only right after an e-mail step, it goes waitHours (default 24, min 1) after the person opens that e-mail and is skipped when it is not opened within fallbackDays (default 5). Opens are approximate (Apple Mail and security scanners). Omit to keep the step's current condition. To change the days of no_reply_days, move the step (toDay).

day.description: The day of the step (for add: the new day), or "last" for the final step.

interaction.description: linkedin_like only: what the LinkedIn interaction does. like (default, "Curtir post"), like_comment, visit or reply_comment; see the channel's description. like_post is accepted as an old name of like with commentFallback false. With add (channel linkedin_like) it is what the new step does; with change on a linkedin_like step, its new interaction.

op.description: change (default) rewrites a step's text; add inserts a step; remove deletes one; move changes its day; condition changes what lets it go (condition).

outroDecisorFallback.description: change and add: Only on a step whose text cites {{outroDecisor}}: the whole sentence that replaces the one citing it for a person whose company has no other decision maker found, e.g. 'Oi, {{firstName}}, isso é algo que você olharia ou tem outra pessoa aí que cuida disso?'. It may use {{firstName}} and {{company}}, never {{outroDecisor}}. Omit it to let Nock say it without a name. "" takes it off; omitted keeps it.

ownPostsOnly.description: Old name, kept for compatibility: true is commentFallback false, false is commentFallback true. Use commentFallback.

recentDays.description: linkedin_like with like ("Curtir post"), like_comment or reply_comment only: how many days back a post or comment counts as recent (7 to 90; 30 for a new Curtir post and for like_comment, 14 for replies when omitted; a Curtir post saved before with none keeps 60). With change on a linkedin_like step, its new window.

variantB.description: change and add: Version B of this step for an A/B test: each person gets version A (body) or version B, and the version with the higher reply rate becomes the step's only text once both went to enough people. Saved with the exact text given, never rewritten. subject only for e-mail steps (omitted: the e-mail keeps version A's subject). Not for a LinkedIn connection request nor a linkedin_like step. Saved on the campaign's template, never on one person's messages. A change may carry only variantB (body omitted): version A stays as it is. null removes the step's version B; omitted keeps it.

prospectId.description: Prospect UUID, read only with scope one_person.

requestedDays.description: The days of the steps the request asks to change (the step open on the user's screen when the request does not say), or "all" for a change of form or tone or a change to every message. Edits on any other day are refused.

scope.description: template (default): the shared template and everyone on it. one_person: only prospectId's messages.

steps.description: Full replacement cadence in send order. Use edits instead to change a few steps.

Leave empty only for a LinkedIn connection request without a note, and for linkedin_like.

Keep each step's branch as the campaign has it; a cadence sent without branches, with a LinkedIn message waiting for the accept before e-mails, gets the paths by itself.

No follow step exists.
